mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >25 bps in 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below a 12-month moving average triggers a negative demand shock, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 12-mo moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates a broad-based contraction in manufacturing activity, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-mo moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a precautionary savings behavior, which reduces aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises AND GDPC1 falls for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 1% for more than 12 months in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-mo moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages for two consecutive months signals a synchronized demand expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-mo moving average AND HOUST > 12-mo moving average for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
